title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling policies will cover legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, policy activation requirements, licensing and governance controls are supported by the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. It correctly distinguishes automatic support in new policies from the edit and rerun needed for existing policies, and reports preview completion after the roadmap's November target month.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The change is admin-opt-in: existing policies need an edit and rerun, while administrators creating new policies get legacy support automatically.
claims.quote: New auto-labeling policies will automatically support these file formats. ... Existing auto-labeling policies require a small policy edit and another policy run to restart the crawl and evaluate legacy Office files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends simulation and review before enabling a new or updated policy.
claims.quote: Before enabling a new or updated policy, run it in simulation mode and review the results to confirm that it identifies the intended content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The change expands the files that policies can evaluate and label according to their rules.
claims.quote: The change expands the files that auto-labeling policies can evaluate and label to include legacy .doc, .xls, and .ppt files in SharePoint and OneDrive, according to the request.

claims.claim: The labeling impact is limited to legacy files in the SharePoint and OneDrive locations covered by the policy.
claims.quote: Review your sensitivity labels and auto-labeling policies, including the SharePoint and OneDrive locations in scope. ... Identify the policies for which you want to extend coverage to legacy Office files.

claims.claim: An encrypting label used by a policy covering SharePoint or OneDrive must use Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: For an encrypting label used with SharePoint or OneDrive, User access to content expires must be Never.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: Auditing must be turned on for auto-labeling simulation.
claims.quote: Auditing is turned on for Microsoft 365. Required for simulation.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive before policies can label files there.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive. Required before any label can be applied to files in those locations.

claims.claim: A label used to label files must have a scope including Files & other data assets.
claims.quote: To label files, the label scope must include Files & other data assets.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling is not currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible in the Purview portal when the tenant cannot support the functionality.
claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: A policy can be turned on through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Mode Enable enables the identified policy for actions and notifications.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy. ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications is a policy test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: Policy locations are configured through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... select the Edit policy button. ... For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSiteLocation> adds a SharePoint location to an explicitly scoped policy.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter is available to add OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: The policy editor is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... For a policy in the Off section, select the Edit policy button.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Comment <text> sets an optional comment on the identified policy.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... The Comment parameter specifies an optional comment. If you specify a value that contains spaces, enclose the value in quotation marks

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the PowerShell Comment edit restarts the crawl for legacy Office formats in the same way as the notice's policy-edit procedure.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview legacy Office files Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy Comment restart crawl'; read MC1530948 and the Comment and StartSimulation reference sections; searched the reference for legacy, restart and crawl; simulation restart is stated, legacy-format crawl restart is not.

claims.claim: Auditing can be enabled through Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns auditing on.
claims.quote: Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The auditing-enable command is run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Items to review displays the emails or documents matching the policy's simulation rules.
claims.quote: For policies in simulation mode, select the Items to review tab to see which emails or documents matched the rules that you specified.

claims.claim: Without Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator, Turn on policy is greyed out even after successful simulation.
claims.quote: Without one of these roles, the Turn on policy button appears greyed out even after a successful simulation.

claims.claim: Administrators govern the legacy-format capability through auto-labeling policies and the existing policy and auditing controls documented in the table.
claims.quote: Admins manage the capability through Microsoft Purview auto-labeling policies. Microsoft Learn identifies the Microsoft Purview portal's Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies surface for service-side auto-labeling.

claims.claim: The supplied notice identifies organizations using service-side auto-labeling in SharePoint and OneDrive as affected and does not mention Exchange.
claims.quote: Who is affected ... Organizations using Microsoft Purview service-side auto-labeling policies for files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive
